# `•special` — Special functions

`•special name` returns the special function called `name`, as SciPy names it, with SciPy's order of arguments. For a list of names, `•special` returns a list of functions.

```bpl
[erf gammaln]←•special "erf" "gammaln"
erf 0.5                ⍝ 0.5204998778
gammaln 5              ⍝ 3.17805383
```

Each function works item by item on real numbers and gives floats, as `⊛` does. Exact numbers and integers are converted to floats.

| Name | Call | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `"gammaln"` | `gammaln x` | ln \|Γ(x)\| |
| `"digamma"` | `digamma x` | ψ(x), the derivative of ln Γ(x) |
| `"polygamma"` | `n polygamma x` | ψ⁽ⁿ⁾(x), the nth derivative of ψ, for a whole n |
| `"erf"` | `erf x` | the error function |
| `"erfc"` | `erfc x` | 1 − erf x, without the loss of digits for large x |
| `"erfinv"` | `erfinv p` | the x with erf x = p |
| `"beta"` | `a beta b` | B(a, b) = Γ(a) Γ(b) ÷ Γ(a + b) |
| `"gammainc"` | `a gammainc x` | the regularized lower incomplete gamma function P(a, x) |
| `"betainc"` | `[a b] betainc x` | the regularized incomplete beta function Iₓ(a, b) |

`betainc` takes its shape parameters a and b as one pair on the left. For arrays of pairs, apply it with Rank, which pairs each row of the left argument with an item of the right.

```bpl
[pg bi]←•special "polygamma" "betainc"
1 pg 1                          ⍝ 1.644934067
[2 3] bi 0.5                    ⍝ 0.6875
[2 3◇4 5] bi¹ ⁰ 0.5 0.25     ⍝ 0.6875 0.1138153076
```

`∂` differentiates each function with respect to its last argument. The slope of `gammaln` is digamma, the slope of digamma is `1 polygamma`, and the slope of `n polygamma` is `(n+1) polygamma`. `∂` also differentiates `beta` with respect to a. `∂` raises `UNSUPPORTED` for a slope with respect to the order of `polygamma`, the a of `gammainc` or the pair of `betainc`:

```bpl
[erf bi]←•special "erf" "betainc"
erf∂ 0.5                ⍝ 0.8787825789
{[2 3] bi ω}∂ 0.5       ⍝ 1.5
```

`0 polygamma x` is digamma. For a whole n from 1 to 170, `n polygamma x` has a result for any x above 0. A result too large for its float kind is `∞` or `¯∞`, as `170 polygamma 0.5` is.

An unknown name, a name that isn't a string or a complex argument raises `DOMAIN`. A call with the wrong number of arguments raises `SYNTAX`. A left argument of `betainc` that isn't one pair raises `LENGTH`.

Under dynamic kinds, `digamma`, `polygamma`, `erfinv`, `beta`, `gammainc` and `betainc` raise `DOMAIN` when non-NaN arguments produce NaN. This includes digamma at a negative integer and incomplete beta outside its domain. Under [static kinds](../numbers.qmd#static-kinds), these numeric checks are disabled and NaN is returned. Infinite results do not raise an error.
